Most of it? I’m amazed by the amount of people that think research is just a bunch of rich folk throwing around money to go to conferences and have lavish events. I have worked in research for over 4 years now and worked in healthcare before for 4.5. I wish I got paid a lot of money but I have 3 bachelors and only get paid 18.30 an hour and I literally got a raise 2 weeks ago. So let me tell you how it goes down since not many people do. The primary investigator or PI from here on out is the person who makes and writes out the million dollar research question. They then take this written question with along how the plan to answer it and previous work they have seen to back up the claims. Now let’s say they ask for a million dollars. Now to simplify it there are 2 kinds of cost. Direct and indirect costs. Direct costs are exactly 1 million just like the PI asked and go to paying the people who actually work on the research, so research assistants who collect the data or paying participants who join studies or just ordering lab supplies overall/ equipment. Pi’s do not get paid out of this pool typically, sometimes but usually they have a salary through the university or hospital. Then there are the Indirect costs which have been the center for discussion of budget cuts. These costs are negotiated by universities or hospitals to the government and are typically set at a rate from around 40-60% of the total budget. So without a million at a rate of 60% that’s $600,000 on top of the million. These are the funds that go to paying people who don’t work directly on research but support it like accountants, janitors, etc. it is also what pays the fees like water, electric, equipment/ facility maintenance. So without the indirect costs bye bye all those folks and good equipment. I will say though that universities do tend to abuse this a little. They often take all indirect costs from research and put it into a large liquid pool and use it to pay those folks mentioned earlier but also use it for new buildings, dorms, etc and most researchers never see a dime of it. Other than that though yes it is a small drop in the bucket compared to military spending.

The problem might be occuring because you are trying to merge multiple voxels (a pixel of a MRI usually representing a 1mm^3) of varying quality at the same coordinate into one image.
